newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX August power ekes out gain in choppy session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX August power ekes out gain in choppy session.

text.p: NYMEX August electricity futures managed small gains Wednesday in a choppy session, which initially rose on rumours and eventually found support from firm natural gas and western physical prices.
"The cash market is strong so people are reluctant to sell," a broker said about a spate of buying toward the close.
August Palo Verde (PV) electricity futures settled up one cent at $34.67 after fluctuating between $34.50 and $35.50.
September PV finished down 29 cents at $28.38. Deferred PV contracts ended 10 to 15 cents lower.
August California-Oregon Border (COB) settled up nine cents at $21.62 after bouncing in a 30 cent range.
September COB finished down two cents at $21.81. Other COB months ended down 10 to up five cents.
The complex was bolstered early by rumours of operational problem at one of three 1,221 megawatt (MW) units of the Palo Verde nuclear power plant in Arizona. market sources said.
Those early gains were erased when Palo Verde's operator Arizona Public Service Co said the three units were working normally at full output.
Strength in the western cash prices and natural gas futures continued to provide support for the power complex, brokers and traders said.
Day-head firm, peak power prices at PV rose five dollars to $44.00-47.00 a MWh, while those at COB eased slightly to $17.00-18.00.
NYMEX August Henry Hub natgas futures settled up 1.2 cent at $2.174 per million British thermal units.
Short-term physical prices traded steady to higher on unplanned plant outages and heavy energy demand for cooling in the interior part of the Southwest, market sources said.
The 750 MW Mohave coal-fired unit 3 was shut Monday for repairs and expected to resume operation Saturday.
Restart of the 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming was delayed to Thursday from today.
The 254 MW Valmy coal-fired unit 1 in Nevada will unlikely return to full power until the weekend after its output was halved Tuesday because of a tube leak.
While the two San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) units in San Clemente. California, were in a startup mode, neither was sending power to the grid Wednesday morning.
The 1,070 MW SONGS unit 2 expected to synchronize with the regional power grid later today, and the1,080 MW unit 3 was scheduled to be place online tomorrow.
In Richland, Washington, output at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant climbed to 73 percent earlier today.
Forecasters called for normal temperatures to continue across the Pacific Northwest into next week, and hot but seasonal weather over most of the Southwest.

Although prospects of front-month prices remained bearish as more generation is due back by next week, selling pressure will likely be mitigated in the short-term by strong natgas and cash power prices, market sources said.
"I don't see anyone is going to push it down hard until gas and daily prices come off," a Houston futures trader said.
Separately, southbound capacity of the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie transmission system will be cut by 250 MW to 3,200 MW between 0900 and 1600 PDT on Thursday and Friday for maintenance work.
NYMEX estimated 902 PV and 337 COB contracts were sold.
((--R Leong, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622))
